relations.subject: Betty Heimann
relations.evidence: She immediately began the study of classical philology, Indian philology and philosophy at the Christian-Albrechts-Universität zu Kiel.

relations.subject: Betty Heimann
relations.evidence: In Kiel she studied with Paul Deussen (1845-1919) and with Emil Sieg (1866-1951).

relations.subject: Betty Heimann
relations.evidence: On 4 January 1921 she successfully submitted her dissertation to Emil Sieg at the University of Kiel, receiving her doctorate.

relations.subject: Betty Heimann
relations.evidence: Her teachers included Hermann Oldenberg at the  University of Göttingen, Hermann Jacobi at the University of Bonn, and Sten Konow at the University of Hamburg.

relations.subject: Betty Heimann
relations.evidence: She accepted a position as an assistant and librarian to the professor of classical Semitic studies in Kiel from 1921 to 1923.

relations.subject: Felix Jacoby
relations.evidence: Felix Jacoby was a professor of classics at Kiel

relations.subject: Friedrich Otto Schrader
relations.evidence: Friedrich Otto Schrader became a professor of indology there in 1921.

relations.subject: Betty Heimann
relations.evidence: habilitated there in Indology on 1 November 1923, with Eugen Julius Theodor Hultzsch (1857-1927).

relations.subject: Betty Heimann
relations.evidence: Heimann moved to the Martin-Luther-Universität Halle-Wittenberg (University of Halle) as of 1921 and habilitated there in Indology on 1 November 1923

relations.subject: Betty Heimann
relations.evidence: As of 1923 Betty Heimann was the first woman to be a private lecturer at Halle.

relations.subject: Betty Heimann
relations.evidence: As of 1 April 1926 she was appointed to a special lectureship for Indian philosophy at the University of Halle.

relations.subject: Betty Heimann
relations.evidence: As of 11 August 1931 Betty Heimann was appointed as an associate professor (professor extraordinarius) at the University of Halle, filling a position previously held by Eugen Hultzsch.

relations.subject: Betty Heimann
relations.object: School of Oriental and African Studies at the University of London
relations.evidence: She was able to obtain work teaching Indian philosophy on a freelance basis at the School of Oriental and African Studies at the University of London.

relations.subject: Betty Heimann
relations.role: half-time position in the Department of Indian Philosophy
relations.evidence: For some time she held a half-time position in the Department of Indian Philosophy at the University of London, which was created specifically for her.

relations.subject: Betty Heimann
relations.object: School of Oriental and African Studies at the University of London
relations.role: Professor of Sanskrit and Indian Philosophy
relations.evidence: After World War II in 1946 she was appointed as a full-time senior lecturer,  Professor of Sanskrit and Indian Philosophy in the School of Oriental and African Studies at the University of London.

relations.subject: Betty Heimann
relations.evidence: From 1945 to 1949 Heimann was a professor at the University of Ceylon in Colombo, Ceylon (later the University of Colombo, Sri Lanka).

relations.subject: Betty Heimann
relations.object: Department of Sanskrit at the University of Ceylon
relations.evidence: Heimann was the founding head of the Department of Sanskrit at the university.

relations.subject: O. H. de A. Wijesekera
relations.evidence: Her successor as professor of Sanskrit was O. H. de A. Wijesekera, who had been one of her students at the University of London.
